top.title: Messi’s defending champions Miami knocked out of MLS Cup playoffs
top.description: Columbus Crew, with an injury-time goal from Santiago Rodriguez, beat Lionel Messi’s Inter Miami 1-0 to knock the defending champions out of the first round of the MLS Cup playoffs on Friday. Rodriguez’s goal in the second minute of stoppage time gave Columbus a 2-0 triumph in the best-of-three first-round series, after their stunning 3-0 victory in game one in Florida. The defeat was a season-ending disappointment for the star-studded Miami side that features Messi, Luis Suarez, Casemiro and Rodrigo De Paul, which also came up short in the CONCACAF Champions Cup and the Leagues Cup. For Argentine superstar Messi, MLS’s top scorer in the regular season and the favorite to win an unprecedented third straight Most Valuable Player award, it was a second first-round exit in the three MLS Cup playoffs he has contested. Miami, facing a must-win game after dropping the opener at home to seventh-seeded Columbus, had chances to score on a cold, rainy night in Ohio. German Berterame had a golden opportunity six minutes from full time, but his header from point-blank range went over the crossbar. The match appeared headed for a penalty shootout with injury time ticking away. But Inter’s defense allowed Rodriguez to bring down a cross in the box from Moroccan Anass Zaroury and blast it past Canadian goalkeeper Dayne St. Clair. Miami’s early exit extends the champion’s curse in MLS. No team has retained the title since the Los Angeles Galaxy in 2012. top.title: 49ers' Mac Jones wouldn't have minded a trade. A tradeoff? He gets to start vs. Seattle
top.description: Quarterback Mac Jones started eight games for the 49ers last season while Brock Purdy was hurt. Jones will get the start Sunday against the Seahawks while Purdy recovers from an ankle injury. (Ryan Sun/Associated Press) Mac Jones will start for a franchise Sunday that he was at least halfway hoping would get rid of him less than three weeks ago. On Friday, when asked about the interest he generated before the NFL's trade deadline on Nov. 10, the San Francisco 49ers backup quarterback was candid. Did Jones think it sounded more appealing to start for a playoff contender in need of a QB rather than keep collecting dust behind Brock Purdy ? "Yeah, definitely have thought about it," Jones said. "And I was just glad that the deadline was over because I got to move forward." On Sunday, Jones will move into the starting lineup with Purdy sidelined with a sprained left ankle. And Jones will have a chance to show why the 49ers have declined to deal him after his brilliant 2025 relief work made him an appealing trade target. After playing 20 mop-up snaps this season, Jones' first real action will be a real challenge: He'll face the Seahawks' top-ranked defense at Levi's Stadium with rain in the forecast. Jones, 28, noted he long ago gained NFL experience playing in wet conditions against a formidable foe. On Oct. 3, 2021, in his fourth career start as a rookie, Jones faced Tampa Bay, then the defending Super Bowl champions, and QB Tom Brady in Brady's only game against New England, his employer for his first 20 seasons. Jones completed 31 of 40 passes for 275 yards with two touchdowns and an interception in a 19-17 loss in a downpour. "That was like the game of the century," Jones said, laughing. "And I wasn't freaking out about the rain. I just went out there and played. So that's what I'm going to do this time." Jones' work last season gives the 49ers confidence he can deliver on the promise. Jones went 5-3, ranked second in the NFL in completion percentage (69.6), 12th in yards per attempt (7.4) and 13th in passer rating (97.4) among the 36 QBs who had at least 200 pass attempts. In his final start, a 42-26 loss to the Rams, he became the third QB in franchise history to complete 30-plus passes with a completion percentage of at least 80%, joining Steve Young and Jeff Garcia. In his penultimate start, a 34-24 road win against the Giants, he completed 19 of 24 passes, and he joined Young and Joe Montana as the only QBs in franchise history to complete at least 14 consecutive passes to start a game. top.title: USWNT winners and losers: Emma Hayes' side clinch 2027 World Cup berth in 8-0 rout of El Salvador as Ashley Sanchez makes roster statement with hat trick
top.description: Ashley Sanchez Ashley Sanchez stole the show with a hat trick, while Lily Yohannes pulled the strings in midfield as the USWNT secured World Cup qualification in emphatic fashion. The U.S. Women's National Team took care of business against El Salvador in Mansfield, Texas, on Friday night, cruising to an 8-0 win and securing a direct berth at the 2027 FIFA Women's World Cup. It took just nine minutes for the U.S. to open the floodgates, with center back Kennedy Wesley making a late run into the box to put the Americans on the scoreboard. Despite committing six defenders to the back line, El Salvador struggled to contain the USWNT in the box. The U.S. scored six more goals before halftime, with Ashley Sanchez leading the way with a hat trick. The second half was a quieter affair, but Croix Bethune added an eighth as the Americans continued to dominate, finishing the match with 78 percent possession compared to El Salvador's 22 percent. Emma Hayes' side can now confidently check World Cup qualification off their list. And while the USWNT's attacking display stole the show, the Americans were equally commanding defensively, not allowing a single shot on target. GOAL looks at the Winners & Losers from Texas Health Mansfield Stadium in Mansfield, Texas. WINNER: Ashley Sanchez The pressure has been on Sanchez to deliver for the national team. The midfielder enjoyed the best NWSL season of her career, scoring 20 goals for the North Carolina Courage and earning league MVP honors. Sanchez earned her second straight national team call-up, and despite limited minutes in two promising appearances against Spain, she still had work to do to secure a spot on the World Cup roster. On Friday, Sanchez took her role in midfield in stride and executed it almost flawlessly. She led the U.S. with a hat trick, and none of her three goals were simple tap-ins. She made quick runs to the far post, evaded pressure and used delicate touches in tight spaces to create narrow windows to shoot. There was no shortage of standout attacking performances for the USWNT on Friday night, but Sanchez's was the most impressive. If she can continue translating her club form to the international stage, she'll be difficult for Hayes to leave off her World Cup roster. LOSER: El Salvador's backline El Salvador played with six in the back against the United States in the Concacaf W Championship. El Salvador knew they had a massive test ahead of them against the four-time World Cup champions. top.title: ‘In a weird way’: Mason Rudolph shares how the Aaron Rodgers drama actually helped Steelers beat Broncos
top.description: Photo by Lauren Leigh Bacho/Getty Images The Pittsburgh Steelers capped off a very difficult week with a fine win over the Denver Broncos. The drama surrounding Aaron Rodgers, who was released earlier this week, dominated the headlines, and many felt that would have an impact on the team. However, the Steelers were incredibly dominant, beating the Broncos 27-5. Mason Rudolph says the Aaron Rodgers ‘adversity’ brought the Steelers together Mason Rudolph hadn’t been involved in first-team reps all week, which is why he had to put in extra work on Thursday ahead of Friday’s game. The quarterback, who took over Rodgers’ role, definitely played his part, delivering a clean, efficient and turnover-free game-manager performance. Unsurprisingly, the questions after the game were always going to be dominated by the Rodgers saga during the week. Rudolph was asked about it too, and he claimed that the controversy helped, as it brought the team a lot closer ahead of the win against the Broncos. He said on Prime Video: “It was a lot. Sort of unprecedented, nothing I’ve ever been through and probably the same for all my teammates. “We’re so proud of the way we turned the page on Wednesday, and the veteran leadership – Cameron Heyward, Jalen Ramsey, T. J. Watt – really led us forward.” Rudolph further added: “I think the leadership council just sort of rallied around Coach McCarthy. And I think, in a weird way, you know, the adversity brought us probably closer together. And I think we’ll just keep carrying that into week after week.” The 31-year-old hadn’t started a game for over a year, so the pressure was on for him to deliver after taking Rodgers’ place against the Broncos. Rudolph finished the game with nine of 15 passes completed (60.0%) for 142 yards and one touchdown. He took a sack for a 12-yard loss, which was really the only blemish in his performance, while posting a 113.8 passer rating. All in all, it was a fine outing for the Steelers after what has been a tough week. We’re sure Rudolph and everyone else will be delighted with how the game panned out. top.description: Ashley Sanchez needed just six minutes and 27 seconds to score a hat trick, helping the United States women’s national team dismantle El Salvador in the quarterfinals of the Concacaf W Championship on Friday, securing a place at the 2027 FIFA Women’s World Cup in Brazil. For all the attacking power head coach Emma Hayes assembled in her starting lineup, it was her center backs who got the scoring underway first in front of a crowd of 6,595 at at Texas Health Stadium in Mansfield, Texas. Kennedy Wesley opened the scoring in the ninth minute, finishing Mallory Swanson’s cross. Tierna Davidson doubled the lead at the half-hour mark, finishing another Swanson pass, just before Swanson added a third goal moments later. Then came the Sanchez show. The North Carolina Courage midfielder, coming off an MVP-winning NWSL season with a golden boot under her belt, scored in the 37th minute, and again in the 39th and completed a hat trick in the 43rd. Sophia Wilson set up one goal while Alyssa Thompson provided the other two assists. Wilson wrapped the first-half scoring in the 45th minute, finishing a pass from captain Lindsey Heaps to give the U.S. a 7-0 lead in the first 45 minutes. For Sanchez, Friday night in Mansfield, Texas, was the continuation of a remarkable comeback. Before returning to the USWNT in October against Spain, the 27-year-old had gone 710 days without a call up to the national team. Her goal against Spain in Philadelphia, Penn. was her first international goal since 2022, when she scored against Costa Rica in the previous Concacaf W Championship, helping the USWNT qualify for the 2023 Women’s World Cup and the 2024 Paris Olympics. Hayes made a handful of substitutions in the second half, bringing Croix Bethune, Jadyn Shaw, Michelle Cooper and Sam Coffey in for Wilson, Swanson, Thompson, Lily Yohannes. Bethune, who won NWSL’s midfielder of the year award and broke the single season assist record before lifting the NWSL trophy with Kansas City Current last weekend, scored the eighth goal in the 80th minute, finishing Heaps’ assist with a smooth placement into the back of the net. But perhaps as interesting as the scoreline was Hayes’ selection for the first qualifying match of her tenure since winning the gold medal in Paris in 2024. With Trinity Rodman unavailable due to shoulder injury, Hayes opted for a starting XI that relied mostly on NWSL standouts: attacking trio of Swanson, Wilson and Alyssa Thompson, with Yohannes, Sanchez and Heaps in midfield, Emily Fox, Gisele Thompson as fullbacks, Davidson and Wesley as center backs and Seattle Reign’s Claudia Dickey in goal. top.title: Somers ends a magical season for Burnt Hills-Ballston Lake football in state semifinals
top.description: The Burnt Hills-Ballston Lake football team's season ended with a state semifinal loss to Somers on Friday in Middletown. (Jim Franco/Times Union) MIDDLETOWN - The Burnt Hills-Ballston Lake football team put in plenty of work this season, which resulted in the Spartans tripling their win total from 2025. But on Friday evening, the Spartans' incredible turnaround season came to a crushing conclusion. The Spartans could not get anything going of consequence during the first half of the their Class A state semifinal showdown against top-ranked Somers. Meanwhile, the Tuskers produced touchdowns on all four of their offensive series in the first half and cruised to a comfortable 35-7 victory at Middletown High School. Ty Starr made sure the Spartans were not shut out when the senior took a handoff and swept off the left side for a 56-yard touchdown run with 18 seconds left in the game. "They are a really good team. We played our hearts out - everyone throughout the team, and that is that," BH-BL senior linebacker Logan Tomlinson said. "At the end of the day, they won. Good for them. Have them go win it all. We fell short." Somers (13-0) is a program with four Class A state titles to its credit since 2016, including three straight championships from 2022 to 2024. The Tuskers proved too tough for BH-BL to contain during the first half as the Section 1 champions produced touchdown drives covering 62, 81, 98 and 61 yards in establishing a 28-0 halftime cushion. "We always talk about life. Life isn't perfect," BH-BL coach Kevin DeBonis said. "We just lost to a very good team. We came out uncharacteristic. We stubbed our toes with assignments. That's what happens. Unfortunately, they exposed that. They are a very good team. It is hard to go down like that. It was sort of an avalanche early on." This season's squad ended up matching the program record for wins in a season with 12, a standard first established in 2009 and matched by the state championship squad from 14 years ago. "We had the biggest bounce back (season) of my life," Tomlinson said. "At the end of the day, we won 12 games. If we didn't do that, I would be a little bit more upset." nigeria.title: Messi’s defending champions Miami knocked out of MLS Cup playoffs
nigeria.description: Columbus Crew, with an injury-time goal from Santiago Rodriguez, beat Lionel Messi’s Inter Miami 1-0 to knock the defending champions out of the first round of the MLS Cup playoffs on Friday. Rodriguez’s goal in the second minute of stoppage time gave Columbus a 2-0 triumph in the best-of-three first-round series, after their stunning 3-0 victory in game one in Florida. The defeat was a season-ending disappointment for the star-studded Miami side that features Messi, Luis Suarez, Casemiro and Rodrigo De Paul, which also came up short in the CONCACAF Champions Cup and the Leagues Cup. For Argentine superstar Messi, MLS’s top scorer in the regular season and the favorite to win an unprecedented third straight Most Valuable Player award, it was a second first-round exit in the three MLS Cup playoffs he has contested. Miami, facing a must-win game after dropping the opener at home to seventh-seeded Columbus, had chances to score on a cold, rainy night in Ohio. German Berterame had a golden opportunity six minutes from full time, but his header from point-blank range went over the crossbar. The match appeared headed for a penalty shootout with injury time ticking away. But Inter’s defense allowed Rodriguez to bring down a cross in the box from Moroccan Anass Zaroury and blast it past Canadian goalkeeper Dayne St. Clair. Miami’s early exit extends the champion’s curse in MLS. No team has retained the title since the Los Angeles Galaxy in 2012. nigeria.title: INEC tests BVAS, result portal today
nigeria.description: By Omeiza Ajayi The Independent National Electoral Commission, INEC, will today run a nationwide mock accreditation and result transmission exercise in all 36 states and the Federal Capital Territory (FCT), about seven weeks before the 2027 general election. INEC Chairman, Professor Joash Amupitan, disclosed this at the INEC and Office of the National Security Adviser, ONSA) Strategic Election Security Conference in Abuja on Thursday. He said the exercise would put the Commission’s new equipment and result systems under live conditions. “While this exercise allows INEC to stress-test our upgraded BVAS devices and verify our stricter INEC Result Viewing Portal, IReV, v,lidation safeguards—which automatically block arithmetic inconsistencies and over-voting, it also serves as an essential live dry run for our security architecture,” he said. The presidential and National Assembly elections hold on 16 January 2027 across 177,299 polling units, with governorship and State Houses of Assembly elections to follow on 6 February 2027. Amupitan said the Commission had procured new accreditation machines and set a lower voter threshold for the actual election in January. “INEC will deploy over 1.41 million ad hoc personnel alongside 57,000 newly procured Bimodal Voter Accreditation System (BVAS) devices, calibrated at a reduced threshold of 850 voters per machine,” he said. He told the gathering that the rehearsal was as much a test of coordination with security agencies as of technology. “Strategy without rehearsal is merely aspiration,” he said. The INEC chairman called on the Commission’s Resident Electoral Commissioners and the Commissioners of Police in the states to take part fully. “I urge all Resident Electoral Commissioners and Commissioners of Police to treat November 28 as a full-scale operational rehearsal: test your communication lines, evaluate rapid-response times around mock polling centres, and identify any logistical or security blind spots while there is still ample time to resolve them,” he said. INEC had earlier published the list of polling units selected for the nationwide mock accreditation exercise, naming 17,656 locations across the 36 states and the Federal Capital Territory FCT. The commission said the exercise is a “Mock Accreditation and Result Upload Exercise” using the Bimodal Voter Accreditation System, BVAS. nigeria.title: Death on the River: Some who came for rescue were more interested in stealing phones, bags, money — Survivor
nigeria.description: By Emem Idio, Yenagoa Survivors and bereaved families of the November 20 boat tragedy in Bayelsa State have recounted their horrifying experiences, describing how passengers struggled for survival as the overloaded vessel capsized, leaving several people, including children, dead. The boat was conveying mourners from Ayama to Ukubie Community in Southern Ijaw Local Government Area of the state for a burial ceremony when the tragedy occurred. One of the survivors, Mrs Lucy Africanist Olugbo, an indigene of Ijo-Gbanraun who is married in Ukubie, described the ill-fated vessel as an old boat that was unfit to carry the large number of passengers. Olugbo, who was travelling to attend the burial of her husband’s half-sister, said the passengers had initially expected to travel in a speedboat, but when none was available, a local boat was brought to convey them. She said the boat started making cracking sounds shortly after boarding, raising fears among some passengers. According to her, the vessel began tilting from one side to another, forcing passengers to shift their weight in the same direction and further destabilising it. She said water had started entering the boat while it was still moving, creating panic among the passengers. Recounting how she escaped, Olugbo said she secured a bag around her neck before pushing a heavy-set woman forward and jumping into the river. She said when she resurfaced, she saw men, women and children struggling desperately in the water. The survivor also alleged that some youths who arrived in boats, apparently to assist in the rescue operation, were more interested in collecting passengers’ phones, money, bags and other belongings than rescuing those struggling in the water. She said she personally witnessed four elderly women and a young lady die in the incident. Another survivor, Mrs Mary Silas, said she travelled with seven members of her household, including her children, younger sister and younger brother. Silas said she was particularly worried because one of her sons could not swim, prompting her to approach the boat driver and appeal to him to stop and allow some passengers to disembark. She said, “The boat was shaking and making strange sounds. Because I was travelling with my son who could not swim, I became very worried. “I approached the driver and told him that there were many children and people who could not swim on board. I told him that since we were close to the riverbank, he should stop and allow some people to come down. “He told me, ‘Okay, madam, I have heard you.’ But to my surprise, instead of stopping, he sped into the middle of the river. People were shouting, and before we knew what was happening, the boat collapsed and started sinking.” Narrating how she managed to save herself and her children, Silas said she used her swimming skills to guide her son through the water. Some of the political parties that will be on the ballot have already hit the streets campaigning. Many of the candidates are seeking to renew the mandate that was given to them in 2023. Others who didn’t make it in the last election are back again hoping to succeed this time around. The candidates are making fresh promises. The electorate, on their part, have been speaking on what will inform their choice of who to vote for during the elections and their responses reveal an electorate pulled in sharply different directions. We did not embark on data collation but randomly spoke with some Nigerians in the southwest, southeast, south south and the northern region of the country. Backers of President Bola Tinubu defend him on his capacity to push restructuring and take bold decisions, arguing that but for him the economy would have collapsed completely, even as some concede that his reforms have yet to ease hardship. But they have hope and argue that Nigeria would be better under Tinubu in the years to come. A few voices break from the Obi-Tinubu argument entirely, backing Atiku, the ADC, or local candidates on performance. Many voters express lack of faith in the process and expect politicians to rig and litigate rather than accept the people’s verdict, even as the spate of ongoing violence is already scaring them. Professionals frame their choices more cautiously arguing that they will be guided by candidates’ positions on sustainable development, Niger Delta equity and resource justice rather than ethnicity or party. nigeria.title: Manhunt launched for killers of NSCDC officer in Benue
nigeria.description: By Peter Duru, Makurdi The Chairman of Agatu Local Government Area of Benue State, Mr Melvin Ejeh, has vowed to ensure the arrest and prosecution of those responsible for the killing of an officer of the Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps (NSCDC), Inspector Anyebe Anya. Anya was reportedly killed by armed men who attacked him at his duty post at a checkpoint in Agatu a few days ago. The assailants were also said to have carted away his service rifle after the attack. Ejeh gave the assurance when he visited the deceased officer’s family in Otukpo to commiserate with them, describing Anya as a hardworking, honest and dedicated officer. He vowed that those behind the killing would not escape justice, assuring the bereaved family that efforts were already underway to track down and apprehend the perpetrators. “Those that killed him will not go unpunished. We will get all of them. I knew him personally. He was a very hardworking, honest man who was committed to his work. “The whole community is mourning his death. The people of Agatu are shocked and grieving over his death. “We console his family. He was a committed officer. I can assure you that we will get those involved and they will be brought to justice. There is a hunt for them already. “The entire Agatu people will not rest until he gets justice, that I can assure his family,” the chairman said. nigeria.title: Meet Emmanuel Emegha, Chelsea’s new striking sensation who has Nigerian roots
nigeria.description: By Enitan Abdultawab Chelsea’s latest attacking prospect, Emmanuel Emegha, is already giving supporters reasons to pay attention after scoring against Nottingham Forest on Friday. While the Blues trailed by two goals to nil, the 23-year-old striker, who joined Chelsea from French side Strasbourg, came off the bench to replace Danny Welbeck, found the net in the 54th and 89th minutes, and offered the Blues a lifeline in their Premier League encounter. However, his goals were not enough as Forest held unto their lead after Morgan Gibss-White had extended it immediately after, bringing the game to a 3-2 full-time result. Before the Forest clash, Emegha put Chelsea ahead at home when they hosted Leeds United last week. Unfortunately, he could not save the team from capitulating to a 1-4 defeat in the game. But beyond his growing reputation in England, Emegha has an interesting connection to Nigeria. Born in The Hague, Netherlands, to a Togolese father and a Nigerian mother, the powerful forward has West African roots. His Nigerian heritage makes him a player of interest to Nigerian football fans, particularly those following the growing number of players of Nigerian descent making waves in European football. However, Emegha has chosen to represent the Netherlands internationally. He made his senior debut against Poland in November 2025, explaining that the Netherlands is his country and that he is proud to be Dutch. Although Nigeria missed out on having him represent the Super Eagles, his progress at Chelsea gives Nigerian fans another reason to follow his career closely. At 23, Emegha has the physical presence, pace and goalscoring instincts to make an impression in English football. His latest goals against Nottingham Forest are another early signs of what he could offer Chelsea. nigeria.description: Nottingham Forest claimed a memorable 3-2 victory over Chelsea at the City Ground on Friday night, November 27, piling further pressure on Blues manager Xabi Alonso after another disappointing performance from his side. nigeria.description: INEC tests its systems on Saturday. Opposition leaders face their own test on Monday. Campaign violence makes both exercises more consequential. By Tuesday, Nigerians should have fresh evidence about two institutions seeking their confidence. INEC will have conducted its nationwide mock accreditation and result-upload exercise. Opposition parties will have had their scheduled opportunity to formalise cooperation in Abuja. The first must demonstrate operational readiness. The second must demonstrate an ability to act together. Both approach those tests amid a worsening concern: whether citizens can participate in the campaign safely. Wednesday’s attack on Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) supporters in Benin City, Edo State, confirmed by the police, followed Monday’s deadly violence in Delta. Edo police reported one person injured and ordered an investigation. The attackers’ political affiliations and any sponsors have not been established. Saturday: Let The Test Produce Evidence INEC’s mock exercise is scheduled for November 28, from 8:30 a.m. to 2:30 p.m. Nigerian time, in 17,676 selected polling units. It will test accreditation, election devices, and the uploading and viewing of simulated results. Registered voters in the selected units are expected to participate. The most useful outcome would be a public account of performance. How many locations opened on time? How many participants were successfully accredited? Where did devices fail? nigeria.title: Two Nigerians arrested over romance scam in Thailand
nigeria.description: Two Nigerian men have been arrested in Thailand over their alleged links to an international romance scam network targeting victims across Southeast Asia. The suspects, aged 41 and 30, were arrested on November 18 at a condominium in Ban Mai, Pak Kret district, Nonthaburi, following an investigation by Thailand’s Immigration Division 3 and Provincial Police Region 1. According to local media outlet, The Thaiger, undercover police officers disguised themselves as food delivery workers to gain access to the suspects’ apartment. With the help of security guards, the officers approached the condominium and pretended to have a parcel for delivery. When one of the men opened the door, they identified themselves as police officers and moved in to arrest both suspects. A search of the apartment reportedly led to the recovery of laptops and mobile phones containing messages linked to fake online identities posing as US military personnel. Investigators suspect the identities were used to establish romantic relationships with potential victims as part of an international scam operation. Police also reportedly found social media accounts allegedly created to deceive Thai residents. The arrests followed an earlier investigation on November 12, when police detained another Nigerian man, aged 37, at Owl Market in Nonthaburi over suspected links to the same network. Investigators later searched a condominium in Bang Kraso, Mueang Nonthaburi, where suspected members of the group had reportedly stayed. However, the men had left before the search. Police subsequently traced the two suspects to another condominium in the Muang Thong Thani area, where they were believed to have stayed for two to three days before their arrest. The Thaiger reported that both men confessed during questioning. However, the charges publicly reported against them are immigration-related offences, including illegal entry and unauthorised residence. One of the suspects, aged 41, had reportedly overstayed his permitted stay in Thailand by 411 days. Authorities revoked their permission to remain in the country and transferred them to Pak Kret Police Station for further legal proceedings ahead of deportation. The investigation into the suspected romance scam network is ongoing. Thai police have not disclosed the identities of the alleged victims, the amount of money involved or the specific roles the two men allegedly played in the operation. A small number of networks remain paused for maintenance, which Binance called standard practice and said was unrelated to the hack. The update closes out a month of phased reopenings. Binance confirmed the breach on Oct. 29, saying its initial investigation pointed to a compromised DevOps engineer’s laptop that gave the attacker access to a service container, which was then used to submit unauthorized withdrawals. The world’s largest crypto exchange stopped all customer withdrawals for two days after the theft, Reuters reported . When they first reopened, customers pulled a net $4.7 billion off the platform, Binance said on Nov. 2. Binance covered the losses Binance said on Nov. 12 that it had completed coverage of the affected assets with more than $6.34 billion of company funds. The money came from a partial draw on its Secure Asset Fund for Users, part of its futures insurance fund and its corporate treasury, and the exchange pledged to rebuild SAFU to about $1 billion. Starting Nov. 27, clients of VTB’s brokerage can trade cryptocurrencies in the VTB My Investments app, the broker said . For now, the trades happen over the counter rather than on an exchange, and access is limited to qualified investors, the legal term for Russians who meet wealth or experience thresholds, who also pass the new test. “In our model, access to cryptocurrencies will require qualified investor status and passing special testing,” Andrei Yatskov, head of brokerage services at VTB, said . He said the test would appear in the app on Nov. 27 and work like the bank’s existing tests for other instruments. VTB handles the buying, storage and record-keeping itself on Russian infrastructure. To trade, clients need to open a separate digital account at VTB’s digital depository, where the crypto is held, on top of their regular brokerage account. The bank received its digital depository and crypto exchange licenses on Oct. 6. “At the start, we will focus on buying and selling cryptocurrencies, and then we will introduce additional services as regulation develops,” Yatskov said. Eight questions before the first trade The launch came quickly after the regulator moved. On Nov. 26, the Bank of Russia approved the first basic standards for brokers and crypto exchange offices, setting the rules for the test. Every investor has to take it, qualified or not, and it is free. Buyers must answer at least seven of eight questions correctly. The standard lays out eight topic blocks, from regulation, technical basics and information security to stablecoins, low-liquidity coins, address labeling and blocked transactions, and volatility, with one question drawn at random from each. Investors who fail can try once more the same day, with different questions. Brokers are barred from sharing the correct answers with clients or telling them which questions they missed. A passing result stays valid for one year from the test date or the latest trade, whichever comes later. The test was the missing piece for Russian banks. When retail buying became legal on Nov. 17 , T-Bank said it was waiting on a market standard for testing, and VTB said it was waiting on the remaining rules. business.description: Bitcoin Magazine Bitcoin Price Trades Near $61,300 as Tech Stock Futures Rally The bitcoin price traded near $61,300 on Friday morning, as tech stock futures jumped ahead of a holiday-shortened session on Wall Street. Bitcoin price is on track for its first weekly gain after seven straight weekly losses, though it is still down about 20% in November. The bitcoin price was up about 1.7% early Friday and set to add 4.8% for the week, Investing.com reported , extending a recovery from a two-year low of $57,325.70 hit earlier in the week. Bitcoin slumped below $57,500 on Wednesday as the Nasdaq sank at the open, before a late rebound in tech shares lifted risk assets. Short sellers helped fuel the bounce. Shorts made up 77% of $84.7 million in bitcoin liquidations over the past day, while futures open interest was little changed. That suggests forced short covering, rather than fresh leverage, supplied much of the lift. Tech futures lead the risk rebound Nasdaq 100 futures rose 2.2% by 6:42 a.m. ET, Reuters reported, as investors returned from Thanksgiving and piled back into battered AI-linked shares. Nvidia gained 3.6% in premarket trading, while AMD climbed 4.4% and Broadcom added 3.4%. S&P 500 futures rose 1.6%, and Dow futures gained 1.3%. “There have been some signs that the tech selloff has stabilised for now, and that risk appetite is returning to markets,” Deutsche Bank analysts said in a note cited by Reuters. entertainment.description: Young man with a hard hat holding a red for sale sign outside a building by Pavel Danilyuk for Pexels . My parents’ generation mostly bought land the way their parents did. Someone in the family knew someone in the village. An uncle walked the boundaries. The community remembered who owned what, and if anything went wrong, you had a face to go back to. However, my generation buys land on Instagram. I do not say that to mock anyone. I sell land for a living. When I started in real estate sales in 2023, two years after finishing a Mathematics degree at the University of Ibadan, I assumed buyers would care most about price and location. They do care. But what I hear most often is fear, dressed up as questions. Can I trust you? Is this land real? What happens if I miss a payment? After I pay, will someone come and ask me for more money? A prospective buyer once asked me, before anything else, whether community or family payments would follow after she paid for her plot. She was not asking about the land. She was asking whether the price I quoted was the real price. She had good reason to ask. Lagos State’s Property Protection Law of 2016 made it an offence to demand levies for construction on someone else’s property. Yet the same law still allows a land-owning family, with the family head’s authority, to collect a customary fee for possession, the payment many people know as a “foundation levy”. So the honest answer to her question is not a simple yes or no. It depends on the land, the family, and what has been written down. Most first-time buyers have never been told any of this. That is the gap I keep coming back to. Nobody taught us how to buy land. We learned how to save. Some of us learned how to invest in stocks, crypto or a side business. But land, the asset our parents spoke about with the most respect, has no manual. The people who used to stand in for the manual–the uncle, the community, the family lawyer everyone trusted–are often not part of how we buy anymore. So we improvise. She was checking whether I was consistent, whether my posts matched what I said on the phone, whether I had been around long enough to be real. I was flattered. Then I was worried. entertainment.description: What makes a good teacher? Beyond knowing a subject, a good teacher can understand students, inspire confidence, and help young people discover what they are capable of becoming. It was this broader responsibility of educators that Dr. Tunji Olowolafe explored while delivering the 2026 Convocation Lecture at the Sikiru Adetona College of Education, Science and Technology (SACOETEC), Omu-Ajose, Ogun State. Speaking on Monday, 23 November 2026, on the theme “The Dual-Mandate NCE-Degree Programme: Prospects, Challenges and the Future of Teacher Education in Nigeria,” he described the programme as an important opportunity to reposition teacher education. For decades, Colleges of Education depended on university affiliations to award Bachelor’s degrees, despite many possessing the academic capacity to run such programmes. The Federal Colleges of Education Act 2023 changed this, empowering eligible institutions to award degrees independently. Under the Dual-Mandate programme, students can complete three years of NCE training and proceed to another two years for a Bachelor’s degree in Education. Dr. Olowolafe explained that combining practical teaching skills with deeper academic knowledge would produce better-prepared educators. However, he cautioned that institutional autonomy must be supported by sustained funding, improved curricula and professional development. With Nigeria facing an estimated shortage of one million teachers, he also called for greater integration of vocational education, artificial intelligence and digital skills into learning. “AI can explain a quadratic equation at midnight, but it cannot offer the steady, empathetic guidance of a caring adult,” he said, emphasizing that artificial intelligence must complement, not replace, the human qualities of effective teaching. During the lecture, Dr. Olowolafe announced that the Tunji Olowolafe Foundation would establish a fully equipped, solar-powered Gbemisola Olowolafe Memorial ICT Centre (GOMTECH) with high-speed internet connectivity at SACOETEC. The Foundation is also committed to recognising academic excellence and outstanding teaching at the College. This includes recognising the College’s first-class degree graduates and NCE distinction holders, alongside the overall best NCE and degree graduates. Lecturers, selected based on student ratings, will also be honoured for their teaching contributions. The initiative builds on the Foundation’s existing investment in education, including Project Digi-Teach at Ekiti State University and GOMTECH in Are-Ekiti. For Dr. Olowolafe, the commitment to educators is also deeply personal. His mother was a teacher, his elder sister taught for years at Baptist Academy, Lagos, and his late wife, Gbemisola Olowolafe, was a lifelong educator. He recalled the influence of teachers who shaped his own experience, particularly Mr. Soewu of Methodist Boys’ High School , whose patience helped students understand difficult concepts without humiliation. For generations of Nollywood viewers, Pete Edochie was the actor they could recognise before he had even finished his first sentence. He became one of Nigerian cinema’s most familiar faces, often playing kings, chiefs, fathers and respected elders. entertainment.description: After more than 30 years of experience in the fashion industry, the entrepreneur is bringing her experience to a Nigerian clothing brand built on a simple proposition: quality should not have to come at an exorbitant price. In fashion, the conversation often begins with style, but it rarely ends there. Quality, affordability, accessibility and the story behind what we wear are increasingly becoming part of how consumers make their choices. For Alero Ebigbeyi, these are not just considerations; they are the principles shaping her latest venture, HÉYCH. The Nigerian fashion and clothing brand officially opened its retail store on November 10, bringing together fashion enthusiasts, media executives, influencers, friends and industry personalities for an introduction to the brand and its collections. Guests explored the space, examined the clothing and made purchases. Yet, amid the excitement of the launch, two observations kept coming up: the quality of the pieces and their affordability. It was a response that reflected the thinking behind HÉYCH, a brand seeking to occupy an important space in the market by making well-made, stylish clothing accessible without asking consumers to compromise on quality. For Ebigbeyi, this approach is informed by more than three decades of experience in the fashion industry. Having spent over 30 years understanding the business of clothing, she brings to HÉYCH a perspective that extends beyond trends and aesthetics to the practical realities of production, pricing and delivering value. “One thing that sets HÉYCH apart is that we do not compromise on quality, and we are equally intentional about making our products affordable. With over 30 years of experience in this industry, I understand the importance of quality, production standards and delivering value to customers,” she says. Rethinking How Fashion Is Produced That understanding is reflected in one of the brand’s most significant decisions: its investment in local manufacturing. Behind HÉYCH’s retail offering is a manufacturing facility in Lagos, a strategic investment that gives the brand greater control over production while creating the capacity to fulfil orders in large quantities. For Ebigbeyi, local production is as much about business efficiency as it is about building something sustainable within Nigeria. entertainment.title: Nollywood Legend Pete Edochie Passes Away at 79
entertainment.description: Nollywood icon Pete Edochie, MON, who passed away at the age of 79 in Enugu. Photo Credit: Pete Edochie/Instagram Nollywood and the wider African entertainment community are mourning the loss of one of their most respected screen icons, Pete Edochie , MON, who passed away on Wednesday, 25 November 2026,at the age of 79. According to an official statement released on behalf of the family by his eldest son, Leo Pete Edochie , the veteran actor and retired broadcaster departed this life at 12:30 a.m. in Enugu, Nigeria, following a protracted battle with prostate cancer. Born on 7 March 1947 in Zaria, Kaduna State, and hailing from Akamnato, Ifite Nteje in Anambra State, Pete Edochie began his career in broadcasting long before becoming a household name on television and cinema screens. At age 20, in 1967, he joined the Eastern Nigeria Broadcasting Service (ENBS)—later the Anambra Broadcasting Service (ABS)—rising steadily through the ranks to serve as Director of Programmes and Deputy Managing Director. His defining breakthrough came in 1987 when he portrayed the fierce, tragic hero Okonkwo in the Nigerian Television Authority’s (NTA) acclaimed television adaptation of Chinua Achebe ‘s Things Fall Apart. His commanding presence and deep, resonant voice earned him international recognition—including a dedicated delegation interview from the BBC—and cemented his place in Nigerian television history. Over a screen career spanning nearly four decades, Pete Edochie became synonymous with authority,traditional wisdom, and unforgettable Igbo proverbs. Whether playing stern monarchs, principled elders, or complex patriarchs, he delivered every line with unmistakable gravitas. His extensive filmography includes standout appearances in classics and modern hits alike, such as Things Fall Apart (1987), Igodo (1999), Egg of Life (2003), Oracle (2003), Billionaires Club (2003), End of Money (2005), Lionheart (2018)—where he starred as Chief Ernest Obiagu alongside Genevieve Nnaji—Unroyal (2020), and Foreigner’s God (2022). In recognition of his immense contributions to Nigerian arts and culture, he was conferred with the national honour of Member of the Order of the Niger (MON) in 2003 by former President Olusegun Obasanjo,alongside the Africa Magic Viewers’ Choice Awards (AMVCA) Industry Merit Award and lifetime achievement honours from the Africa Film Academy and the African Film Festival (TAFF). sports.description: Quarterback Mac Jones started eight games for the 49ers last season while Brock Purdy was hurt. Jones will get the start Sunday against the Seahawks while Purdy recovers from an ankle injury. (Ryan Sun/Associated Press) Mac Jones will start for a franchise Sunday that he was at least halfway hoping would get rid of him less than three weeks ago. On Friday, when asked about the interest he generated before the NFL's trade deadline on Nov. 10, the San Francisco 49ers backup quarterback was candid. Did Jones think it sounded more appealing to start for a playoff contender in need of a QB rather than keep collecting dust behind Brock Purdy ? "Yeah, definitely have thought about it," Jones said. "And I was just glad that the deadline was over because I got to move forward." On Sunday, Jones will move into the starting lineup with Purdy sidelined with a sprained left ankle. And Jones will have a chance to show why the 49ers have declined to deal him after his brilliant 2025 relief work made him an appealing trade target. After playing 20 mop-up snaps this season, Jones' first real action will be a real challenge: He'll face the Seahawks' top-ranked defense at Levi's Stadium with rain in the forecast. Jones, 28, noted he long ago gained NFL experience playing in wet conditions against a formidable foe. On Oct. 3, 2021, in his fourth career start as a rookie, Jones faced Tampa Bay, then the defending Super Bowl champions, and QB Tom Brady in Brady's only game against New England, his employer for his first 20 seasons. Jones completed 31 of 40 passes for 275 yards with two touchdowns and an interception in a 19-17 loss in a downpour. "That was like the game of the century," Jones said, laughing. "And I wasn't freaking out about the rain. I just went out there and played. So that's what I'm going to do this time." Jones' work last season gives the 49ers confidence he can deliver on the promise. sports.title: WSU defeats Idaho 69-61 in the 281st Battle of the Palouse
sports.description: Washington State held on to defeat Idaho 69-61 in the 281st Battle of the Palouse. Beasley Coliseum saw a nice Black Friday crowd for the 4-3 Vandals and 3-4 Cougars, as I am sure quite a few folks made their way over from the tailgate lot (and from Moscow). Kase Wynott was making his return to Beasley Coliseum after spending his last two seasons with the Cougs, coming in averaging 17 PPG on 50% FG. The opening minutes were choppy for both sides, as it was only 8-6 Cougs going into the first media timeout. Neither team had much rhythm on offense, and three of the Vandals’ points came via a banked long ball from the top of the arc. The Cougs picked it up in the next segment of the game, pulling out to a 16-9 lead. Jamari Phillips continued to show his versatility on both ends of the floor and his tough shot-making on offense. A 2-11 start from the floor for the Vandals and a 12-5 rebounding advantage for the Cougars were helping a sluggish WSU offense. WSU’s defense continued to stifle Idaho as the Cougs pulled out to a 20-11 lead. With 7:57 to go in the half, the Vandals still only had two makes. But fouls were piling up on the Cougs, with 8 fouls. The Cougars took a 28-15 lead into the under-four-minute timeout. Nine of Idaho’s 15 points were from the free-throw line. Washington State was 11-for-22 from the floor but only 1-6 from three. Kase Wynott came alive at the end of the half with a personal 8-0 run and impressive shot-making to pull the Vandals within four at the half. Idaho was a cool 7-24 from the floor in the first half but went to the line 13 times and converted 11. They came into the game as the seventh-worst free-throw shooting team in the country. WSU led the rebounding battle 21-14 and points in the paint 20-2. The Cougs took a 40-37 lead with 15 minutes to go. The game got really sloppy for WSU in the first ten minutes of the second half. The Vandals claimed the lead for the second time with 11:51 to go. Washington State was 1-11 from three and started to let Idaho get on the boards. Wynott already had 19. This game was fairly unwatchable with the way it was being officiated, but the Cougs didn’t do a lot to help themselves. Amid all the fouls, Mohamed Sankhe was called to action for Washington State, and despite some productive minutes in the first half, he missed the front end of two 1-and-1s. Idaho had a few chances to recapture the lead, but faltered on back-to-back possessions. From there, the game became a slog, but WSU slowly stretched out a two-possession lead, closing it out 69-61. WSU only made two threes (2-12) but dominated in the paint and went to Ronnie Harrison and Harrell down the stretch to finish this one off. Despite going 4-for-10 from the floor, Harrison finished with 20 points on 11-13 from the line. Washington State won the rebounding battle and the points-in-the-paint battle 34-10. sports.title: NDSU Successfully Debuts New QB vs. SJSU
sports.description: LAS VEGAS, NEVADA - OCTOBER 10: Preston Brown #0 of the North Dakota State Bison runs against Kal-El Togafau #44 of the UNLV Rebels at Allegiant Stadium on October 10, 2026 in Las Vegas, Nevada. (Photo by Louis Grasse/Getty Images) Getty Injuries finally caught up with North Dakota State senior quarterback Nathan Hayes after 11 games this season. His oblique injury kept him out of Friday’s game against San Jose State, so the Bison debuted freshman quarterback Preston Brown in his first career start. Brown started with a bang on a 49-yard touchdown pass to wide receiver Jackson Williams in the first quarter. The Missouri native kept it going in the first half, leading four scoring drives to a 24-7 lead, and he did enough to help the Bison hold on to a 38-31 win in San Jose. Brown went 12-23 for 226 yards and a touchdown versus an interception. He also rushed for 31 yards and a touchdown on 13 carries. His rushing score came when the Bison needed it most in the fourth quarter to make it 38-24, which capped a six-play, 71-yard scoring drive. Brown also had ample support for the running game in his debut with 183 yards and three touchdowns overall. Bison Skill Players Step Up Running back D.J. Scott led the way with 86 yards and two touchdowns on 17 carries. Fellow running back Nyeoti Punni rushed for 34 yards on five carries. Running back Barry Kpeenu also chipped in 16 yards on five carries, and he had a 21-yard reception. Wide receiver Chris Kiel had 12 yards on two carries, and he caught a 51-yard pass. Brown also connected well with Williams in the passing game, as the lead wideout had seven catches for 117 yards and the score. Wide receiver Jordan McCants had a 20-yard reception, and Brown spread the ball around to six different pass catchers overall. NDSU Waits Next NDSU improved to 10-2 overall and will await this weekend’s Mountain West Conference results to see if they land in the title game. Winning helped the Bison if things came down to a tiebreaker based on computer ratings amid a logjam of conference teams with 6-2 league records. The Mountain West championship game is Dec. 4, and the matchup will be known after the UNLV-Nevada game on Saturday. sports.description: It wasn’t pretty, but it was a vintage Northwestern win, as Chris Collins would say. On Black Friday, Northwestern (5-3, 0-0 B1G) went back to its roots, using late-game toughness to prevail over Northeastern (2-6, 0-0 CAA) at home. The ‘Cats were outshot 40.7% to 39.3% and outrebounded 38 to 33, and were down by as much as 10 with eight minutes remaining in the second half. However, they won in the grittiness department, snatching a victory away from the Huskies behind 18 second-half points from Jake West and fiery defense from Northeastern transfer LA Pratt. Northeastern came out the blocks hot, snatching a near-immediate 5-0 lead with a mid-range shot from Rashad King and a triple from Louis Bond. The ‘Cats rallied for five unanswered points on back-to-back possessions three minutes into the contest. A Jack Karasinski three and Okku Federiko tip-in layup evened the score before Bond found a second-chance layup to make it 7-5. Pratt took us into the media timeout with his first deuce, and Angelo Ciaravino took us out with a pair of jumpers that gave the ‘Cats a two-possession lead. King ended the run with a triple and Miles Newton snatched away a steal to give Dorian Grosber an easy slam on the opposite end. A five-minute scoring made Northwestern lead-chasers again, as Newton and Josh Goodwin drilled treys to pad the Huskies’ advantage to seven with 10:40 to play in the first half. Ciaravino ended the dreadful Wildcats rut with a steal and slam at the nine-minute mark, and a Karasinski three soon after drew NU closer, making the score 18-16 with 8:37 to play. Back-to-back scores from Bond and Grosber gave the Huskies some breathing room momentarily, ensuring a four-point lead after Federiko’s layup before the under-eight media timeout. That lead became one after Karasinski drilled this third deep ball of the half. King nullified the Bellarmine transfer’s efforts with a triple of his own and two Northwestern layups, sandwiched by two free throws from Bond, kept things close. The latter of the two became a three-point play for West, making it 27-26 with 4:36 on the clock. It was his first make in five attempts to that point. He’d impact the game in other areas, taking a charge and throwing a lob to Symon Ghai – who got his first career start on Friday – to pull the ‘Cats ahead by one with 3:26 to play in the first half. West put home another two after the last break in the first half, beginning to find a groove. The Huskies wouldn’t let the Wildcats pull away, grinding to get a crucial four points just before the halftime buzzer. sports.title: Somers ends a magical season for Burnt Hills-Ballston Lake football in state semifinals
sports.description: The Burnt Hills-Ballston Lake football team's season ended with a state semifinal loss to Somers on Friday in Middletown. (Jim Franco/Times Union) MIDDLETOWN - The Burnt Hills-Ballston Lake football team put in plenty of work this season, which resulted in the Spartans tripling their win total from 2025. But on Friday evening, the Spartans' incredible turnaround season came to a crushing conclusion. The Spartans could not get anything going of consequence during the first half of the their Class A state semifinal showdown against top-ranked Somers. Meanwhile, the Tuskers produced touchdowns on all four of their offensive series in the first half and cruised to a comfortable 35-7 victory at Middletown High School. Ty Starr made sure the Spartans were not shut out when the senior took a handoff and swept off the left side for a 56-yard touchdown run with 18 seconds left in the game. "They are a really good team. We played our hearts out - everyone throughout the team, and that is that," BH-BL senior linebacker Logan Tomlinson said. "At the end of the day, they won. Good for them. Have them go win it all. We fell short." Somers (13-0) is a program with four Class A state titles to its credit since 2016, including three straight championships from 2022 to 2024. The Tuskers proved too tough for BH-BL to contain during the first half as the Section 1 champions produced touchdown drives covering 62, 81, 98 and 61 yards in establishing a 28-0 halftime cushion. "We always talk about life. Life isn't perfect," BH-BL coach Kevin DeBonis said. "We just lost to a very good team. We came out uncharacteristic. We stubbed our toes with assignments. That's what happens. Unfortunately, they exposed that. They are a very good team. It is hard to go down like that. It was sort of an avalanche early on." Burnt Hills-Ballston Lake, making its 11th state playoff appearance since 2006, hasn't reached the final since claiming the program's first state championship in 2012. A win would have sent the Spartans to the title game for the fifth time and the first with DeBonis as head coach. This season's squad ended up matching the program record for wins in a season with 12, a standard first established in 2009 and matched by the state championship squad from 14 years ago. "We had the biggest bounce back (season) of my life," Tomlinson said. "At the end of the day, we won 12 games. If we didn't do that, I would be a little bit more upset." BH-BL will bring back 30 juniors from its 2026 squad. DeBonis lauded his senior's contributions and added how proud he was regarding his squad's second-half showing Friday. "Kudos to the kids. sports.title: SB Nation Reacts Results: The Seat Should Be A Little Warm
sports.description: GREEN BAY, WISCONSIN - NOVEMBER 15: Head Coach Kevin O'Connell of the Minnesota Vikings looks on before the game against the Green Bay Packers at Lambeau Field on November 15, 2026 in Green Bay, Wisconsin. (Photo by Todd Rosenberg/Getty Images) | Getty Images A little earlier than usual, we have the results of our SB Nation Reacts poll for this week about our Minnesota Vikings, so let’s go ahead and give you those, shall we? Yes, we shall. Our first question, as always, was whether or not you are confident about the direction of our favorite team. . .and, after hitting a season high as far as our confidence number is concerned, we are underwater once again. Yes, ladies and gentlemen, we are down to just 42% of our readers who think the Minnesota Vikings are heading in the right direction after taking a pretty lopsided loss against the San Francisco 49ers in Mexico City. I can understand being a little down after losing by four scores in prime time, but still. . .this team is 7-3 and should be on their way to the postseason in the NFC, so it’s difficult to be that down. I think it is, anyway. But, as always, your mileage may vary. Our second question of the week has to do with head coach Kevin O’Connell, namely whether or not you think he should be on the hot seat. For the majority of you, it appears that you think he should be. Of those who responded to our poll, a full 60% believe that the seat that O’Connell is sitting on should be at an elevated temperature. Another 22% believe that it should not, while another 16% would like to reserve judgement until the end of the season. The other 2%. . .well, they just don’t know. Now, to be clear. . .Kevin O’Connell is a successful head coach. In terms of winning percentage, he’s the most successful head coach in team history. He even has a higher winning percentage than Bud Grant as things stand right now (.625 for O’Connell, .608 for Grant, regular and post-season combined). But as has been pointed out multiple times over the past week or so, pretty much every time this team has gotten themselves into a big spot over the past few years, particularly in prime time, they have looked woefully unprepared. At some point, you have to ask why. . .and, at some point, you would think that it has to come back to the head coach. Will it? Probably not before the end of the season. But if this team makes the playoffs and gets trounced again, there are going to be a lot of questions being asked. Those are our SB Nation Reacts results for this week, ladies and gentlemen. Watt in a game against the Denver Broncos on Nov. 27, 2026. -- Ed Thompson / Steelers Now PITTSBURGH — I underestimated these Pittsburgh Steelers. Not in terms of their playing ability — I think we’ve got that pretty well dialed in at this point. The Steelers are a good but not great team, with a very good defense, that is capable of beating almost anyone on its best day and losing to almost anyone on its worst day. Since they first convened in July, they’ve looked a lot like a 10 or 11-win team, and they’re probably still headed for somewhere in that range after beating the Denver Broncos, 27-5 on Friday. But over the last week, that outlook certainly seemed to be in jeopardy. It started when the team was upset by the Philadelphia Eagles on Sunday, a dreadful loss to a hapless-looking team that featured star wide receiver DK Metcalf getting himself ejected. It continued when head coach Mike McCarthy and quarterback Aaron Rodgers came to loggerheads after practice on Tuesday. McCarthy benched Rodgers. Rodgers went nuclear, ripping McCarthy on The Pat McAfee Show , and accusing him of what amounts to coaching malfeasance — sleeping through meetings, skipping practice, not getting to know his defense and more. The scene in the team’s locker room on Wednesday was surreal. The Steelers players were shell-shocked. I didn’t think there was any chance that the team I saw on Wednesday would be able to turn things around in less than two days, with Mason Rudolph filling in at quarterback with two practices under his belt. Pittsburgh Steelers quarterback Mason Rudolph and general manager Omar Khan at practice on Nov. 25, 2026. — Ed Thompson / Steelers Now The downgrade from a well-prepared Rodgers to a thrust-into-action Rudolph felt signifiant, but not nearly as significant as the mental toll of the week’s drama. sports.title: Dreesen confident Upamecano will stay at Bayern
sports.description: Bayern Munich CEO Jan-Christian Dreesen is optimistic that Dayot Upamecano will remain in Munich for the foreseeable future, even as reports continue to link the defender with interest from some of Europe’s biggest clubs. Speaking to Abendzeitung (via iMiaSanMia ), Dreesen was asked about reports that Upamecano’s contract includes a release clause. The Bayern chief executive avoided confirming or denying the details, leaving the speculation unresolved. “Whether, how, and at what amount release clauses exist or not, I’ll leave that open,” Dreesen said. Repo rts have suggested that the French international could have a €65 million release clause that becomes active next summer. That's the outlook from Counterpoint Research's latest Smartphone Market Outlook Tracker , which points to rising memory costs and constrained supplies as continuing pressure on handset makers and buyers. The downturn was particularly sharp in the third quarter: IDC and Omdia estimated year-on-year shipment declines of 22 percent and 20 percent respectively, as rising prices and component shortages squeezed the market. Don't expect things to get better in the short term, as Counterpoint forecasts another 6 percent drop during 2027. But it believes that the market may see a 6 percent rebound in 2028, as memory supplies improve, pricing begins to stabilize, and pent-up demand for replacement phones returns. The 2026 outlook has been shaped by sharply rising component costs, particularly for DRAM and NAND flash. According to IDC , memory costs have risen approximately 350 percent since last year and are still climbing. As Reg readers will be well aware by now, this has been blamed on the memory manufacturers prioritizing output of high-margin chips to go into AI servers and GPU accelerators, creating a shortage of the mainstream components that are needed for devices like PCs and phones. Vendors have responded by raising prices, reducing memory configurations, and withdrawing lower-cost models. As The Register previously reported , memory costs accounted for almost 60 percent of the total bill of materials in sub-$400 smartphones during Q1 of 2026. For 2027, Counterpoint warns the outlook is for continued tight mobile DRAM supply, further price increases for low-power DDR (LPDDR) memory, and limited evidence to suggest short-term capacity increases. "The 2026 decline was initially expected to mark the low point of the cycle, but the memory situation has remained more restrictive than anticipated," said principal analyst Yang Wang. "Mobile memory allocation is still being displaced by AI and server demand, while higher costs are taking longer to move through handset portfolios and retail channels. The result is a much weaker 2027, particularly for lower priced devices and price sensitive markets." Global shipments are forecast to rebound by 6 percent in 2028, but that would bring shipments only roughly back to this year's already shrunken level, rather than hitting the peak of previous years. Counterpoint cautions that the scale of the rebound will depend on how quickly lower component costs translate into retail pricing. A speedy improvement in mobile memory allocation during the second half of 2027 could bring replacement demand forward and swell shipments, but continued competition from the AI market or another round of handset price increases would hinder recovery. technology.title: Bill for Birmingham's Oracle debacle reaches £128M
technology.description: Birmingham City Council faces a £128.1 million bill for its disastrous transition from SAP to Oracle – more than six times the original estimate for a project that contributed to its financial collapse. Papers presented to its Audit Committee this week put the combined cost of the original implementation, which went live in 2022, and this year's reimplementation at £128.1 million, against £19.96 million forecast in the 2019 business case [PDF]. The report , from program director Philip Macpherson, said the project's funding allocation had previously reached £157 million. The report said the new Oracle Fusion system went live in August without any priority-one or "showstopper" issues. "The program has now moved into the Post Go Live Support phase where [it] continues to provide extra support but slowly transitions towards 'Business As Usual' operating procedures," the report said. It is an understatement to say the same was not true of the first attempt to move the council's finance, HR, and payroll systems off its legacy R/3 SAP system to more modern software. The first project started in 2019 and was supposed to go live in April 2021, but was delayed by a year. After the council started to use the system in April 2022, it soon became beset by a series of serious problems. Although the council had planned to implement Oracle "out-of-the-box," it created several customizations, including a bank reconciliation system that failed to function properly. The council struggled to understand its cash position and was unable to produce auditable accounts . It has spent more than £5 million on manual workaround labor . The system move also contributed to it becoming effectively bankrupt , an event it failed to foresee due to the malfunctioning finance system. It later emerged that officials ignored a "red" warning prior to the go-live date. They were explicitly told the system could cause late payments, a failure to collect debt, and incorrect accounting if it went live. Officials gave the go-ahead regardless. The council decided to reimplement Oracle from scratch, while running the current system as best it could and implementing off-the-shelf software CivicaPay , now rebranded as Civica Income Management. Despite the apparently trouble-free relaunch, the true cost to the council is likely higher than the projected £128.1 million implementation bill. For a start, the original £19 million budget was supposed to support the software implementation for schools , but that was excluded from the reimplementation. Secondly, the council expected significant savings from moving to Oracle in 2022 through greater efficiency. The 2019 business case booked £27 million in savings from 2019 to 2031, for example. A 2024 analysis by Audit Reform Lab, based at the University of Sheffield, estimated that the disaster's direct and indirect financial impact, including lost savings and deteriorating tax collection, would reach £216.5 million by April 2026. technology.title: UK government rejects national consultation on AI datacenters
technology.description: The UK government has rejected calls for a UK-wide public consultation on the environmental impacts of AI datacenters, despite a petition attracting more than 39,000 signatures. Campaign group Protect the Wild launched the petition last month, calling for a national consultation that would consider whether further expansion should be restricted, paused, or halted until those impacts are properly understood and addressed. The nonprofit says the petition smashed the 10,000 signature threshold above which a government response is required in just three days, and the total stood at over 39,000 as this article was being prepared. In its response, published on November 23, the government ruled out the requested UK-wide environmental consultation, saying individual projects' impacts should be addressed through the planning process. It pointed instead to a separate consultation on its draft datacenter planning policy, open until January 8, 2027. "Datacenters are vital to the UK's digital economy. They underpin the digital services that people rely on every day, including public services, healthcare and the way people work. They also provide the infrastructure needed to develop and use AI," the Department for Business, Innovation, Science and Trade (BIST) says. "Building more capacity in the UK will support economic growth and innovation, while strengthening national resilience and ensuring the UK is well placed to realize the opportunities presented by AI." But it adds that the government recognizes the environmental impacts of bit barns are real and must be understood and mitigated, and this is one of the reasons why it established the Data Centre Covenant tests. This Covenant, published last month, sets out tests all compute sheds "are encouraged to meet," while "strategic datacenters" are required to meet them to qualify for additional government assistance. The government has yet to define which datacenters qualify as "strategic," saying it will publish further details and eligibility criteria in due course. Qualifying projects could receive help securing power and accelerating planning. Briefly, the Covenant tests are that operators cover any energy costs they create, so that communities do not have to pick up the bill; that they invest in local communities; adhere to the highest environmental standards; create jobs and drive reindustrialization; and provide secure and reliable access to their compute resources. If this has a ring of familiarity, it is because President Trump earlier this year introduced a Ratepayer Protection Pledge , under which hyperscalers and AI companies agreed to protect US consumers from any bill shocks due to the energy and infrastructure requirements of their datacenter projects. It seems that where the US leads, the UK still often follows. technology.title: Lloyds and Bank of Scotland apps fall over on payday
technology.description: Lloyds Bank and Bank of Scotland customers reported problems accessing online banking and transferring money on Friday morning. Reports on Downdetector began rising around 1000 UTC. Lloyds also acknowledged problems on its service status page . A reader who supplied the screenshot below noted the particularly awkward timing: the last Friday of the month is payday for many workers. It's also retail silly season: while Brits don't celebrate Thanksgiving, many UK outlets nonetheless participate in Black Friday sales, meaning storefronts are losing out. Others are concerned with more practical purchases. One customer tweeted that she had "no food at home and cannot shop because I cannot transfer funds from my secondary Lloyds account to my main one. At this point I'm just going to withdraw every penny the moment I'm paid, so much for Internet banking. Never had this years ago." Bank of Scotland, another Lloyds Banking Group brand, reported similar problems on its service status page : " We're aware some customers are having issues with our app and online banking at the moment. We're sorry about this and are working hard to fix it." Earlier this year, a botched overnight software update at Lloyds Banking Group potentially exposed other customers' transaction information to almost 448,000 app users. In a letter to Parliament's Treasury Committee, consumer relationships CEO Jasjyot Singh blamed a defect in the API handling transaction data. The incident affected Lloyds, Halifax, and Bank of Scotland, and prompted goodwill payments to thousands of customers. Lloyds Banking Group said late last year that it had more than 21 million mobile app users and over 23 million digitally active customers. A spokesperson for Lloyds Banking Group told The Register : "We're aware some customers are having difficulty accessing the app this morning. We’re sorry for the inconvenience and are working to get things back to normal as quickly as possible." ®

technology.title: Europe's AI sovereignty push: Lots of cloud, not much silver lining
technology.description: Europe's IT spending is growing more slowly than the global average, according to Gartner, whose analysts warn that the region's push for tech sovereignty faces commercial and technological obstacles. Gartner forecasts European IT spending of $1.57 trillion in 2027, up 9.9 percent from 2026, compared with worldwide growth of 15 percent to $7.35 trillion. For 2026, it estimates spending growth of 20.7 percent in North America and 13.7 percent in China. "The world seems to be racing towards this AI goal of where the large language model provider is going to be, and the race seems to be between North American-based providers and some Asia Pacific providers," John-David Lovelock, Distinguished VP Analyst at Gartner, told The Register . He said Europe had traditionally trailed in IT uptake. "We saw that happen when global sourcing, cloud, and software as a service all came along. It's down to the pushback against the idea of creative destruction," where new technologies replace old ones. Europe's fastest growing categories are datacenter systems, forecast to grow 29.7 percent in 2027, and infrastructure as a service, at 26.7 percent. Even so, Lovelock does not expect Europe to compete with North America and China on AI investment. "For AI provision, Europe is going to be behind, and there won't be a way to catch up," he said. "The AI datacenters, the large language models, the foundational models, the tools and techniques for building out AI are all being centered outside of Europe, but enterprises don't need to do that. So the question becomes: regardless of where the source of the AI is coming from, can the enterprises actually adopt and use it? In one sense, Europe will be behind in the provision of AI, but it need not be behind in the use." The gap nonetheless complicates Europe's push to reduce its dependence on US technology suppliers. The European Union has introduced new rules to encourage tech buyers to favor sovereign tech over the dominant tech vendors, but Lovelock doubts they will move spending much. "Sovereignty is a wonderful flag that we fly on the front of a building. IT is running in the basement. CIOs are not going to buy a second-best solution that costs more simply because it's sovereign. "They are not going to break any laws, but they are not going to make a decision that puts their company in a worse position at a higher cost. While sovereignty gets [vendors] on the list, it doesn't assure that they get purchased," he told us. Earlier this month, Gartner predicted that by 2029, more than 90 percent of EU organizations will have a digital sovereignty strategy, but argued that a fully sovereign technology stack remains out of reach. "The global technology supply chain is too interconnected, and many critical dependencies cannot be replaced at a commercially viable scale," said Bettina Tratz-Ryan, VP analyst at Gartner. ®

science.title: Dropping missiles from orbit? 2 European companies sign agreement to study the idea
science.description:
Julian Dossett is a freelance writer living in Santa Fe, New Mexico. He primarily covers the rocket industry and space exploration and, in addition to science writing, contributes travel stories to New Mexico Magazine. In 2022 and 2024, his travel writing earned IRMA Awards. Previously, he worked as a staff writer at CNET. He graduated from Texas State University in San Marcos in 2011 with a B.A. in philosophy. He owns a large collection of sci-fi pulp magazines from the 1960s.

A pair of companies in Europe have signed an agreement to study the feasibility of developing weapons that can be dropped from orbit. Atmos, a space company known for its Phoenix reusable reentry vehicle , will work with MBDA, Europe's largest missile manufacturer, on the new project. "We are assessing how proven defense systems and new orbital technologies can be combined to strengthen Europe's conventional deterrence and enable future defense capabilities," Sebastian Klaus, the CEO of Atmos Space Cargo, said in a statement on Nov. 18. The system that the companies are investigating is called Precision Orbital Deep Strike, or PODS. The companies said that their initial scope will center on design and feasibility, as well as technology integration. Atmos and MBDA also said this work could lead to demonstrations, but the companies' announcement makes it clear that any deployment or use would be subject to the approval of governmental and military authorities. "The initiative also directly supports MBDA's broader strategic vision in the space domain, reinforcing both space for defense and the defense of space," Thomas Gottschild, MBDA Deutschland managing director, said in the same statement. This news comes a few months after Chief of Space Operations Gen. Douglas Schiess said that the U.S. Space Force operates orbital weapons . "Let me be crystal clear: Today, Guardians operate on-orbit weapons that can defend the joint force against space-enabled attacks," Schiess said during a conferenace presentation on Sept. 15 ("Guardians" refers to Space Force personnel.) Last year, Atmos' Phoenix capsule got its first test run in space. The cargo-return technology launched aboard a Space X Falcon 9 rocket during a rideshare mission in February 2025. Atmos tested out the inflatable heat shields it has been working on to help future space-manufactured cargo make it through Earth's atmosphere in one piece. "Orbital transportation and return form a new layer of strategic infrastructure, and infrastructure determines what Europe can achieve on its own terms," Klaus said in the Nov 18 statement.
